questions.q: Which field must be chosen before Profile on the New User form, because it limits which profiles are available?
options: Time Zone
User License
Mailing Address
Delegated Approver
questions.explain: The User License determines which profiles can even be selected, so it has to be set first.

questions.q: Does the Username field need to be a real, deliverable email address?
options: Yes, Salesforce sends all notifications there
No — it must be formatted like an email address and unique org-wide, but the separate Email field is what needs to be real
No, it can be any plain text string
Yes, and it must match the Email field exactly
questions.explain: Username is email-formatted and globally unique across all Salesforce orgs, but only the Email field needs to be a real, deliverable address.

questions.q: What happens when you deactivate a user?
options: Their record and historical data are permanently deleted
Their login access is removed, but their record and history are preserved
Their username is immediately reassigned to someone else
Their profile is automatically changed to Minimum Access
questions.explain: Deactivation clears the Active checkbox, blocking login while keeping the user record and everything tied to it intact.

questions.q: When would you use Freeze instead of immediately deactivating a user?
options: When you want to permanently delete their account
When deactivation is blocked by a dependency (like a custom hierarchy field) and login needs to stop right now
When creating a new user for the first time
When resetting someone's password
questions.explain: Freeze blocks login instantly and reversibly, which is useful when deactivation can't happen immediately but access needs to be cut off.

questions.q: What is checked by default when you create a new user?
options: Freeze
Active
Delegated Approver
Marketing User
questions.explain: The Active checkbox is checked by default, so a new user can log in as soon as the record is saved.
